correctness.rationale: For n≥5 and 1≤a≤floor((n-3)/2), weight sets {a,b},{a-1,b-1},{a+1,b+1} are pairwise disjoint. R0,R-,R+ consequently have orthogonal inputs and contraction singular values for sufficiently small γ. Projection of each local σ± between Dicke states has amplitude sqrt[w(n-w+1)]/n or sqrt[(n-w)(w+1)]/n; the diagonal ξ filter equalizes both logical amplitudes at sqrt[a(b+1)]/n, proving J=γa(b+1)/n and branch factors p,1-p, while R0 balances no-jump amplitudes at smax. Counting zero-jump A0/B0 patterns gives hypergeometric f_wl and exact cosine D=Mab/sqrt(MaaMbb), with strict D<1 when 0<p<1 by ℓ=0,n ratio separation. Binomial covariance yields 1-D=(b-a)²p(1-p)γ²/(2n)+O(γ³). Independent numerical hypergeometric calculations checked n=5,7,8 at several p and γ, and endpoint equality; this corroborates but does not replace all-n proof.

value.rationale: A natural, physically motivated code family has an exact analytic temperature-independent jump acceptance rate and separately temperature-dependent residual no-jump decoherence, giving a useful restricted-family Pareto choice of excitation gap. The exact jump/fidelity-throughput tradeoff is a meaningful mathematical invariant beyond demonstrating that one five-qubit code has O(γ²) fidelity; no global QEC optimum is implied.

scientific_limitations: The exact D is only the postselected no-jump subchannel under a specified Kraus grouping; not the full corrected channel or basis-independent observable.
Only sufficiently small γ and fixed n for first-order fidelity/acceptance; no unrestricted optimal recovery.
Strong same-model five-qubit PAQEC literature access risk remains.
